title: Notifiers that plug together
description:
Small classes behind one interface can be combined like building blocks.

The interface: `INotifier` with `virtual void send(std::string_view message) = 0;` and a virtual destructor.

Write three implementations:

| Class | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `ListNotifier` | stores every message; `const std::vector<std::string>& sent() const` |
| `PrefixNotifier` | constructed with `(std::string prefix, INotifier& next)`; forwards each message to `next` with the prefix in front. It *decorates* another notifier. |
| `MultiNotifier` | `void add(INotifier& target)`; forwards each message to every target, in the order added. It is a *composite*. |

Because `PrefixNotifier` and `MultiNotifier` are themselves notifiers, they can wrap each other to any depth.
hints: Each class inherits from `INotifier` and overrides `send`. `PrefixNotifier` keeps a reference to the next notifier and calls `m_next.send(m_prefix + std::string{ message })`.
`MultiNotifier` stores `std::vector<INotifier*>` and calls `send` on each in turn. Because all three are notifiers, they can be nested inside each other.
